body:
CANDIDATE 460a14a on m1/chart-eligibility, base c6f1a8b (current main, rebased and re-gated).
Bead bd-01M177SHFXZKMR8K39BPC9K6FF. I hold cost.scala under rv-01M17N8HH49AH9NQTK2MV4CS0T.

This is a defect in work I landed, found by auditing my own carrier rather than by anyone stopping me.

WHAT IS WRONG. The Chart term is produced by ChartDistance.reduction, which measures over
view.structuralMembers(node.ref) - the LEAVES under the node. chartEligible tested node.evidence,
which is the contract of ChartDistance.report: a different function, no view parameter, and one that
genuinely does need a chart on each side. The predicate was written to the wrong function.

They coincide on a leaf and diverge on a segment, and StorySourceView GUARANTEES divergence:
  case NarrativeNodeId.Segment(_) => None // segments never get a fabricated chart
So a segment's own evidence is always None while its leaves carry the charts actually compared.

MEASURED, on segment sc2 with charted leaf e4 and a unit with evidence:
  chart estimate Observed(0.0)     - the term IS measured
  supportWeight 1.0                - the carrier says nothing was assumed
  wChart 0.5, wSensory 0.15
  scaleToEligible 0.9054 (now) vs 1.0405 (correct); supportOf correct = 0.9610

Chart present but not eligible makes wPresent exceed wEligible, so BOTH halves fail the same way:
1. the blend multiplies the cost DOWN. The cell is priced better BECAUSE it measured more - 14.9%
   low against correct scaling.
2. supportOf clamps with min(1.0, _), so an over-unity ratio reports as flat full support.

WHY IT IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. The discount lands only on segment cells and only where charts exist: a
systematic thumb on the scale for coarse anchors over leaf anchors. It would make recall look more
scene-level and gist-like than it is, which is precisely one of the things this system exists to
measure. WOG carries no charts, which is why 204 align tests pass over it. It would have switched on
silently with embed-grakern - a real finding produced by a latent bug, with nothing in the output to
say so.

THE FIX is a strict generalization, not a behaviour change:
  unit.evidence.nonEmpty && view.structuralMembers(node.ref).exists(_.hasEvidence)
leavesUnder returns the node itself for a leaf, so no leaf cell can move. That is a prediction, and
the gate confirms it: NOT ONE expected value anywhere in seven modules changed.
It also gets contradiction right - if every charted member is excluded the term is Missing while
eligibility stays true, which is a genuine missed measurement and should lower support. Structural
already behaved that way. Chart was the odd one out, and Structural was never affected because
structuralEligible never consulted node.evidence.

POSITIVE CONTROL: the law fails on the unfixed predicate with
  "support 1.0 claims nothing was assumed, but Sensory was"
eleven siblings passing. It also asserts its own preconditions - segment, chartless, charted leaf,
Chart actually in terms - because a vacuous law is how the last two defects in this area survived.

GATE: seven modules requested (reference-scope.sh, not chosen by hand), seven totals counted, zero
failures - align 204, codec 107, embedBench 64, embedGrakern 28, fixtures 117, interview 92,
laws 86. scalafmtCheckAll last, clean. Re-gated after rebase, not carried over from before it.

ONE THING WORTH NAMING. The support carrier I built exists to stop a number claiming more than it
measured, and it shipped with the clamp quietly doing exactly that. min(1.0, _) looks like defensive
hygiene and is in fact where the evidence of the bug went: the ratio above one was the symptom, and
the clamp deleted it. I would rather supportOf refused an over-unity ratio outright than clamped it,
because a cell where present exceeds eligible is incoherent by construction, not merely unusual.
I have NOT made that change here - it is a separate decision about whether cost() should be able to
fail, and it belongs to you. Say the word and I will do it as its own candidate.
